Koridori Srbije d.o.o..desc: A Serbian limited liability company set up in 2009 to act as the investor on motorway building, organising the works, running international tenders, carrying out expropriation and preparing project documentation. Its own 2013 status report names four responsible ministries (Transport, Finance, Construction and Regional Development), 104 employees and works worth EUR 1.4 billion then under way on Corridors 10 and 11.

sources.title: Koridori Srbije doo, status overview presented at Danube Region Transport Days (Belgrade)

Public Enterprise Roads of Serbia.desc: The Serbian body that manages the state road network: collecting road-use charges, investing in road building and reconstruction, maintenance, planning and traffic management. It was set up by a Government of Serbia decision of 22 December 2005 (05 no. 023/8228/2005) that took effect on 1 January 2006, with the Republic of Serbia as founder; in December 2025 the government converted it, with six other public enterprises, into a limited liability company.

sources.title: Decision on the establishment of the Public Enterprise for State Roads Management (PE "Putevi Srbije"), Government of Serbia
Seven Public Enterprises Becoming Limited Companies

General Roads Directorate.desc: Albania's national road agency: it plans and contracts road studies, design, supervision and construction, runs road procurement and a technical council that approves designs and cost estimates, maintains road assets and requests the expropriations needed for road building. Albania's state audit office refers to the General Roads Directorate as the former name of the Albanian Road Authority (Autoriteti Rrugor Shqiptar), which operates under Law no. 10164 of 15 October 2009.

sources.title: Mbi Auditimin e Ushtruar ne Autoritetin Rrugor Shqiptar (final audit report, Decision no. 13 of the Chairman of KLSH)

Ministry of Public Works and Housing.desc: Jordan's public works ministry. It builds and develops the national road network linking cities, villages and housing areas, prepares designs and studies for public, village and agricultural roads, designs and supervises government buildings, runs materials testing and quality control, and drafts building and road legislation. Its predecessor department dates from 1923 and it became the Ministry of Public Works in 1954.

sources.title: Ministry of Public Works and Housing - General Information, Jordan e-Government portal

Department of Lands and Surveys.desc: Jordan's land registry and survey department. Under bylaw no. 80 of 1999 it surveys land and fixes boundaries, issues cadastral maps, registers property rights and processes registration transactions, values land for registration, manages and leases treasury land, handles land taken for the public interest, and licenses surveyors and land agents. The government portal traces its origins to the Ottoman land law of 1857.

sources.title: Department of Lands and Survey - General Information, Jordan e-Government portal
The Historical Development of the Department, Department of Lands and Survey

Cameroon Railways (CAMRAIL).desc: The private operator of Cameroon's railway, carrying passengers and freight over the 918 km Transcamerounais line. It took over the state railway Regifercam under a concession in 1999 during privatisation, was a subsidiary of France's Bollore group and now sits under Africa Global Logistics; it says it pays the Cameroonian state about 10 billion FCFA (USD 16 million) a year in taxes and duties and invests about 12 billion FCFA a year.

sources.title: Cameroun: Camrail declare le paiement de 16 millions USD d'impots par an

Hohai University.desc: A Chinese university founded in 1915 and run directly by the Ministry of Education, specialising in water conservancy research and engineering education but also teaching science, economics, management, arts and law. Its own site gave 46,921 students, 3,409 faculty and 19 colleges and departments in 2015.

sources.title: About Hohai University, International School of Hohai University

National Directorate for Water Resources.desc: A national directorate of Mozambique's Ministry of Public Works, Housing and Water Resources, listed as one of the ministry's units by Ministerial Diploma no. 12/2022 of 25 January 2022. It proposes and carries out policy on developing, conserving and using river-basin water, assesses water resources and needs, prepares and monitors basin plans, keeps the register of water uses and the national hydraulic infrastructure plan, runs flood and drought early warning and coordinates on shared international waters. It works through four departments: water resources management, hydraulic works, international water resources and strategic studies.

sources.title: Diploma Ministerial n. 12/2022, Regulamento Interno do Ministerio das Obras Publicas, Habitacao e Recursos Hidricos (arts. 7 and 9)

Energoinvest.desc: A Bosnian engineering company founded in Sarajevo in 1951 that designs, supplies and builds substations, transmission lines, hydro and thermal power plants and water works, mostly as an exporter and lately mainly in Africa and the Middle East. The Federation of Bosnia and Herzegovina government held 67% of its shares as of 2021; before the Yugoslav war it employed more than 54,000 people.

sources.title: Yugoslavia 30 years on: seven decades of Bosnia's red capitalist Energoinvest
Energoinvest d.d. Sarajevo - company and services

Ethiopian Electric Power Corporation (EE.desc: Ethiopia's state-run electricity monopoly, which generated, transmitted and distributed the country's power. It was split into two separate bodies in December 2013: Ethiopian Electric Power, established by a 2013 Council of Ministers regulation under the Public Enterprises Proclamation and tasked with power projects including dams and transmission lines, and a separate service company responsible for operations, distribution and sales.

sources.title: Will Ethiopia sort out its energy puzzle?
Ethiopian Electric Power Establishment Council of Ministers Regulation (entry)

Secretaria dos Recursos Hidricos do Cear.desc: A secretariat of the direct state administration of Ceara, Brazil, created by state Law no. 11,306 of 1 April 1987. It carries out the state water resources policy in an integrated, decentralised and participatory way, coordinates and runs studies, programmes, projects and works on water resources, and links state bodies with federal and municipal ones; its structure was set by state decrees 32,957 (2019) and 33,215 (2019).

sources.title: Sintese do Primeiro Ciclo do Progestao no Ceara (2014-2018), Agencia Nacional de Aguas

Superintendencia de Obras Hidraulicas (S.desc: The water-works executing body of the state of Ceara, Brazil, linked to the state water resources secretariat (SRH) and created in 1987 alongside it. It builds and oversees dams, water-transfer axes, canals, pipelines, wells and water supply systems.

sources.title: Sintese do Primeiro Ciclo do Progestao no Ceara (2014-2018), Agencia Nacional de Aguas

National Mission for Clean Ganga (NMCG).desc: An Indian government body: a society registered under the Societies Registration Act 1860 which the River Ganga (Rejuvenation, Protection and Management) Authorities Order of 10 July 2016 also made an authority under environmental law. It is the nodal agency for implementing that order nationwide, prepares the Ganga basin management plan, sets ecological flows and pollution monitoring, and can issue directions to state and district Ganga committees and local authorities. It has a governing council and an executive committee, its Director General is appointed by the central government, and its accounts are audited by the Comptroller and Auditor General.

sources.title: River Ganga (Rejuvenation, Protection and Management) Authorities Order, 2016 (ss. 31-47)

Office National de l'Eau et de l'Assaini.desc: Burkina Faso's national water and sanitation office, created by Decree no. 85-387 of 22 July 1985 and turned into a state company (societe d'Etat) by Decree no. 94-391 of 2 November 1994. Since 2001 it has held a 40-year public service concession to operate the Ziga dam, whose water is reserved for supplying Ouagadougou and nearby areas, and it is responsible for the dam's upkeep and maintenance.

sources.title: Decret n. 2003-113/PRES/PM/MAHRH/MFB portant concession de service public pour l'exploitation du barrage de Ziga (FAOLEX)

Jiangxi Airport Group.desc: The airport operator for Jiangxi province, China, running Nanchang's airport together with regional airports at Shangrao, Jingdezhen, Ruijin, Ganzhou and Yichun. Over the 1-7 October 2026 national holiday it handled 2,849 flights and 389,000 passengers, 278,000 of them at Nanchang.

sources.title: Guoqing jiaqi Jiangxi jichang jituan yingsong lvke 38.9 wan renci, ge jichang yunxing pingwen youxu
